title: HSM Batched Rotation and Audit Telemetry Playbook (v0.1 draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for orchestrating batched key rotations backed by HSMs, with strong audit telemetry and a Terraform upgrade path for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Target audience: SREs, platform engineers, and security engineers who operate Private Redwood control planes and on-prem inference nodes.

Scope and constraints:
- Covers: scheduled batched rotations, emergency rotations, telemetry schema for audit logs, Terraform module changes for HSM/KMS wiring, and rollback/forensic steps.
- Assumes customers run the Redwood Private control plane with an HSM-backed KMS (PKCS#11 or cloud-HSM proxy).
- Not prescriptive about specific HSM vendor (YubiHSM, Thales, AWS CloudHSM) — vendor-specific notes at the end.
- Goal: rotation with minimal service disruption (<= 2m extra latency per affected node) and deterministic audit trail.

High-level design summary:
1) Batched rotation coordinator (stateless job) triggers rotations per-keystore in configurable batches (default 10 keystores/batch).
2) Each rotation has four phases: PREPARE -> ACTIVATE -> VERIFY -> REVOKE. All phases produce structured telemetry events to the audit pipeline.
3) Terraform modules expose a single opt-in module flag that flips rotation mode from "manual" to "coordinated-batch-v1" and performs safe state upgrades.
4) Fallbacks: synchronous fail-open policy for read-only requests and fail-closed for secret creation until rotation completes, depending on customer matrix.

Telemetry and audit schema (required fields):
- event_id: UUID
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
- rotation_id: UUID (per-batched-run)
- keystore_id: string (customer keystore id)
- key_id: string (HSM key label/slot id)
- phase: [PREPARE|ACTIVATE|VERIFY|REVOKE|ERROR|RETRY]
- actor: service-account or operator user
- terraform_change_id: (optional) PR/Change-id that caused rotation
- outcome: [SUCCESS|FAILURE|PARTIAL]
- details: free text (max 4k)

Emit destinations (examples):
- Primary: customer-managed secure S3 bucket (encrypted) with per-rotation partitioning (s3://redwood-audit/<customer-id>/year=YYYY/month=MM/day=DD/rotation_id.jsonl)
- Secondary: redact-and-forward to central telemetry (Cloudwatch/Stackdriver) for aggregated metrics (counts, latency, errors)
- Local node: ephemeral append-only file (forensic capture) for 24–72h in case of network partition.

Terraform module notes (upgrade path):
- New module: private/kms-hsm/coordinated-rotation (v0.1)
- Backwards-compatible variables:
  - rotation_mode (string): [manual|coordinated-batch-v1] default: manual
  - batch_size (number): default 10
  - kafka_topic (string): optional, if using event-driven coordinator
  - audit_s3_bucket (string): required for coordinated mode
- State migration strategy: add new resource "redwood_rotation_state" as a no-op resource in v0.1 to reserve namespace; migration plan should be run with terraform plan and validated by CI.
- Provider constraints: pin hashicorp/aws >= 4.0 if using cloud-HSM resources; detect on-prem provider setups and avoid creating cloud resources.
- Example snippet (pseudo-terraform):
  module "kms_hsm" {
    source = "github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//private/kms-hsm?ref=v0.1"
    rotation_mode = var.rotation_mode
    batch_size    = var.batch_size
    audit_s3_bucket = var.audit_s3_bucket
  }

Operational runbook (happy path):
1) Schedule rotation window in ticket (JIRA: PD-xxxx) and Slack #private-deployments channel.
2) Update terraform var rotation_mode=coordinated-batch-v1 and apply in staging.
3) Start coordinator in dry-run mode (verify events emitted, no ACTIVATE).
4) Run small batch (batch_size=3) against non-critical keystores.
5) Verify telemetry: every keystore has PREPARE and ACTIVATE and VERIFY events with outcome=SUCCESS.
6) Gradually increase batch_size to target.
7) Post-rotation: confirm agent cache invalidation and that old keys are revoked after customer TTL.

Failure modes and remediation (examples):
- ERROR: ACTIVATE fails due to HSM timeout
  - Immediate: mark keystore as "rotation-failed", coordinator pauses, alert SRE on-call.
  - Remediate: run targeted retry (phase ACTIVATE) after HSM health check, escalate to vendor support if persistent.
- ERROR: VERIFY fails (application rejects new key)
  - Rollback plan: re-issue old key as active (if previously not revoked) or re-route traffic to fallback pool.
- Network partitions: local forensic file used to rebuild events; operator runs reconciliation job to re-sync.

Forensics & evidence collection checklist:
- Collect audit S3 path + rotation_id files.
- Snapshot coordinator logs (correlation via rotation_id).
- Capture HSM vendor logs (PKCS#11 session traces if available).
- Hash and sign artifacts before sharing with security team.

Security considerations:
- No sensitive key material leaves HSM in plaintext in logs. Only key identifiers and SHA256(kid) are allowed in telemetry.
- Audit files must be server-side encrypted (SSE-KMS) at rest; TLS 1.2+ in transit.
- Least privilege: coordinator service account must have Write to audit_s3_bucket and read-only to keystore metadata; HSM operator accounts are separate.
- Retention: default 365 days for detailed rotation logs, 7 years for signed forensic snapshots (customer-configurable).

Vendor-specific notes (short):
- AWS CloudHSM: ensure IAM roles for proxy host are pinned; use CloudHSM cluster failover plan. Verify soft-delete semantics.
- YubiHSM/Thales: validate PKCS#11 version compatibility; test slot enumeration under load.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical event schema for "actor" (service-account vs operator id).
- Add automated snapshotting of HSM state pre-rotation for on-prem (regulatory requirement in some regions).
- Integration test harness: simulate HSM errors (latency, timeouts) in CI.
- Add explicit terraform acceptance tests for state migration.

Appendix: quick checklist for emergency rotation (operator):
- Obtain rotation_id from coordinator UI or runbook generator.
- Set coordinator to single-keystore mode and start with dry-run=false.
- Monitor audit S3 path for PREPARE -> ACTIVATE events.
- If ACTIVATE fails repeatedly, escalate to vendor and apply temporary denial of new secret issuance.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Try batching by geolocation next — reduce cross-AZ HSM chatter.
- Consider lambda-based small-coordinator for air-gapped customers where Kafka is not available.
- Link to test harness: GH PR #512 contains simulation stubs (see linked_artifacts).

End of draft.

-- Daniel
